about: Canonical product vocabulary: one term per concept per locale. `name` is the label form (nav entry, page title, section heading); `item` is the countable noun used in running text. Anchors are message keys that must carry the term (exact, or containing it). Forbidden lists the retired synonyms per locale; `allow` names the few message values that keep one for a stated reason. Display strings only: wire values, routes and enum ids never change with this file. A forbidden entry with `keys` applies only to message keys under that prefix. `decision` records why a concept carries the term it does. `spelling` lists retired spellings per locale. Guarded by src/__tests__/glossary-guard.test.ts. The term covers every form of the concept in display copy: singular, plural and verb phrases ('Medicijn toevoegen', 'Registrar glucemia'), not only the bare noun, so a missing retired synonym is no licence for a second word. A word for a different thing is not a synonym: es 'glucosa' for the analyte (mean glucose, GMI) stays. Every `item` is anchored at least once, or `itemUnanchored` says why it cannot be; every term occurs in its locale's bundle. `short` is the form for a one-line slot (tile, heading, chip, tab), shared with the iOS client; `shortKey` is the message key that carries it, or the full name in a locale without one. A short form is shorter than the name, names one thing, reuses no retired synonym, and reaches a surface only through `metricName` (src/lib/measurements/type-label-keys.ts).

concepts.description: Readings of any metric (weight, blood pressure, pulse ...) and their page.
concepts.decision: The area is Messungen; one value is a Messwert, so capturing one is "Messwert erfassen". Messung stays for the act of measuring (one cuff reading yields several values). Other locales use one word for both.

concepts.description: A medication the person takes; the medications area.
concepts.decision: `name` is the label wherever the concept stands as a label (rail, page title, timeline lane, import kind); `item` is one medication, and the word for counting them. Korean: 복약 as the label, 약 in counts and running text (약 3개). Dutch: Medicatie for the area, medicijn for one medication, the word the copy already used for a single one.

concepts.description: One scheduled or logged amount of a medication.
Recording that a dose was taken; the intake log.
Action: mark a dose as taken. Enforced in detail by i18n-dose-vocabulary.test.ts.
concepts.decision: The daily briefing row for an open dose is the Take action: it opens that dose, highlighted, where Take books it. A client that can book in place may do so on this action; "Einnahme erfassen" / "Log intake" is the name of the form for an unscheduled or backdated intake, not of this action.

concepts.description: Action: mark a dose as skipped. Enforced in detail by i18n-dose-vocabulary.test.ts.
Action: be reminded of a due dose again later.
The preventive-care area at /care: check-ups, visits, procedures, body sites.
concepts.decision: Vorsorge in German; the other locales use the everyday word for a check-up (Controles, Revisiones), which the rail already used, rather than a translation of "preventive care".

concepts.description: One recurring preventive item (a screening, a blood count) and its reminder.
concepts.decision: One reminder type, whoever set it up: a screening, a blood count or a routine the Coach suggests (weigh daily, the 7-day blood-pressure week) sit in the same Vorsorge list and push as Vorsorge-Erinnerung / Check-up reminder. 'Erinnerung zum Messen' and 'Mess-Erinnerung' are retired as names; a sentence may still say what to measure.
concepts.itemUnanchored: The item noun is declined in pl and ru in every message that holds it (o badaniu, об обследовании), so no key carries it verbatim in all locales; the name anchors carry the concept.

concepts.description: A doctor's visit, booked or done (encounter).
concepts.decision: A booked visit is a Termin / cita / appointment-type entry in the rail and the list; "Besuch" and "visita" were only used by the calendar feed and are retired there too.

concepts.description: A prescribed course of sessions (physiotherapy, radiotherapy ...).

concepts.decision: One name for the area in the rail, the page, the settings pages and the timeline lane: what a layperson gets back from the lab is a result, not a lab.

concepts.description: The illness area: illness episodes with symptoms, flares and recovery.
concepts.decision: The area is named for what it holds (Krankheit, Illness), not for a diary format; one record is an episode in every locale, the word the list, the form and the insights already use. The item is the short form the copy uses (Episode); the long form (Krankheitsepisode, illness episode) is for a sentence that would otherwise be ambiguous. Korean uses 아픈 기간, the plain word, and retires the loanword 에피소드.

concepts.description: The card on the illness page that sums up past episodes: how many, how long recovery usually takes.
concepts.decision: Named for what it shows, the person's own course of illness. Not 'Insights', which names the analysis area, and not 'Auswertung'. A compact title may drop the possessive (Krankheitsverlauf, Illness history).

concepts.description: A symptom logged with its strength.
The emergency card (page, offline copy, Wallet pass, QR link).
The anamnesis: history, family history, allergies, emergency information.
Everything recorded about one person; the rail group and the shared record.
The PDF (and FHIR bundle) for a doctor. The PDF header carries this name.

The settings section that builds the doctor report and exports the record. A web settings section: a client that splits the doctor report and the export into other places has no section to name, and keeps its own section names.
The optional HealthLog push relay that carries iPhone notifications.
An iOS Live Activity (Apple's term, translated as Apple does).
A person who looks after a managed profile.
A health record for someone who does not sign in (a child, a relative).
A read-only, passphrase-protected link to the record for a clinician.

concepts.decision: Ruhepuls is the everyday and clinical German word and was already used 43 times against 4; the other locales keep their standard resting-heart-rate term.
Viszeralfett, the compound every other surface already used.

Spanish and Polish use the one-word everyday term (Glucemia, Glikemia) as French, Italian and Portuguese do, already on the dashboard tile, the type name and every threshold; Dutch keeps Bloedglucose, the dominant and clinical form.
The full metric name everywhere it is named, the Coach chip included; Dutch Zuurstofsaturatie, the clinical term the type name and the dashboard already used.

concepts.description: The unit after a pulse or heart-rate value.
concepts.decision: bpm, the international symbol every chart already renders from code in every locale; Russian keeps уд/мин, which its whole bundle uses.

concepts.description: A recorded training session and the page that lists them.
concepts.decision: German Training/Trainings, the native word the bundle already used 79 times and the one every other locale's equivalent matches; Dutch the same (Trainingen). English keeps Workouts.

concepts.description: The button that puts a suggestion off without declining it for good.
concepts.decision: Nicht jetzt, the order five of seven German buttons used.

concepts.description: The flights-climbed metric: floors gone up per day.
concepts.decision: The value counts floors, so it is named for floors as every other locale already did (Stockwerke, Pisos subidos, Beklommen verdiepingen); Treppe stays for stair speed, which does measure stairs.

concepts.description: The morning card about last night.
The morning card about what is different today.
The morning card with what is to do today.
The HealthKit state-of-mind valence (a momentary emotion or daily mood on a pleasant-unpleasant scale), as distinct from the mood log.
concepts.decision: Spanish Estado emocional, the word the mood page already used for this section: Estado de ánimo is the Mood area's name, and one word must not name both. Other locales already keep the two apart.
